**Finding: Deviation (IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data)**

**What I found:**
- **§2(d) (p0029)** is the only true ownership clause and runs one way: "TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface." Vendor ownership of its platform is fine, but there is no counterpart for our side.
- **No ownership or licence provision** covers the work product produced under the §4 Support Services (dedicated programmer deliverables), and there is no statement that we retain rights in Client Content, Client Intellectual Property, or borrower/loan data.
- **§10 (p0063, p0065)** only treats Client's Intellectual Property and "all results of the Hosting and Support Services" as our Proprietary Information — a confidentiality obligation, not ownership.
- **§13 (p0078)** gives incidental comfort ("Client shall retain full ownership of all domains associated with Client and Client Content") but only on discontinuation of Hosting Service.
- **§8(d) (p0054)** grants TrueLink a broad licence to exploit "Credit Data" — noted in the rationale, not redlined: it is a term-limited licence over narrowly defined raw third-party credit data (archived, not combined with Client Proprietary Information) subject to the Non-Competition Agreement, i.e. not an assignment of our data.

Because neither ownership of the deliverables we pay for nor a perpetual licence to them exists, and Customer Data ownership is unaddressed, the clause set fails the fallback.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** inserted a new §2(e) "Client Ownership" immediately after the existing Ownership clause — we retain all rights in Client Content, Client IP and our borrower/loan data; Support Services Work Product is ours with an assignment from TrueLink; a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence covers any embedded TrueLink IP; and no joint ownership is created. TrueLink's Interface ownership is left intact.
